fundamentals.name: Applied Optoelectronics, Inc.
fundamentals.longBusinessSummary: Applied Optoelectronics, Inc. engages in the design, manufacture, and sale of fiber-optic networking products in the United States, Taiwan, and China. The company offers optical modules, optical filters, lasers, laser components, subassemblies, transmitters and transceivers, turn-key equipment, headend, node, and distribution equipment, as well as amplifiers. It sells its products to internet data center operators, cable television, telecom equipment manufacturers, fiber-to-the-home, and internet service providers through its direct and indirect sales channels. Applied Optoelectronics, Inc. was incorporated in 1997 and is headquartered in Sugar Land, Texas.

judgment.summary: Rapidly growing revenue and strong analyst estimates are offset by current unprofitability and high valuation multiples.
judgment.earningsRecap: Last quarter missed EPS estimates by 44.8%; next earnings date is 2026-08-06.
positives: Revenue growth 51.4% YoY and analyst estimates of 109.4% for the current quarter and 441.7% for the fiscal year indicate strong top-line expansion.
PEG ratio of 0.78 suggests that despite a high P/E, growth expectations may justify the current valuation.
Current ratio of 3.83 and quick ratio of 2.85 indicate strong short-term liquidity.
Debt/Equity of 25.36% is relatively low, suggesting manageable leverage.
negatives: Operating and profit margins are negative (-8.6% and -8.5% respectively), indicating the company is not currently profitable.
Return on equity (-6.1%) and return on assets (-3.3%) are also negative, reflecting poor returns on capital.
Free cash flow (TTM) is negative $-445.58M, suggesting the company is burning cash.
Forward P/E of 40.46 and Price/Sales (TTM) of 30.56 are high, indicating a premium valuation.

news.paragraph: Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) has seen significant positive momentum, with shares soaring approximately 10% recently as executives highlight the company's growing role in optics technology. This surge follows analyst reports emphasizing the potential of 800G and 1.6T ramps to drive further stock appreciation, alongside news of doubled Texas capital expenditures driven by major AI and DOCSIS wins. The broader optics sector rally has also lifted AAOI, with the company's stock adding 8% in a single day as part of this trend.
